newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Liberte looses W.African freight capacity.
newsitem.headline: Air Liberte looses W.African freight capacity.

text.p: French airline, Air Liberte, which was put under legal administration last week, has cancelled its Airbus 310-200 passenger services to West Africa, which offered four to five tonnes of freight capacity per flight .
Air Liberte operated twice-weekly frequencies between Bordeaux and Abidjan in the Ivory Coast and between Toulouse and Dakar in Senegal.

"It's a shame that these services have been withdrawn because we were achieving very satisfactory cargo load factors on the routes and were providing some competition for Air Afrique," an Air Liberte cargo official told Reuters.
Air Liberte's long-haul routes from France to the French West Indies and Reunion in the Indian Ocean were continuing as normal, the official said.

"The nine to 11 tonnes of freight capacity on a daily McDonnell Douglas DC10-30 passenger service from Paris to Guadeloupe and Martinique is fully-utilised as is the six tonnes of capacity offered on a twice-weekly DC10-30 passenger service between Paris and Reunion," the official added.
Air Liberte is to withdraw its Airbus 300-600 passenger services between Paris and Montreal from November 2.
On mid-haul flights Air Liberte continues to carry between 500 and 800 kilos of freight per flight on MD83 passenger services from Paris to Casablanca, Agadir, Tunis and Faro, the official said.
On domestic routes, Air Liberte withdrew its Paris-Montpellier and Bordeaux-Nice services from October 1. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
